PixelPop User Guide

Welcome to PixelPop

A small window on your day. PixelPop turns your LED matrix panel into a display that quietly rotates through the things you care about: the time, the weather, your next appointment, a reminder that can’t wait.

PixelPop shows one page at a time on the 64 × 32 panel, then moves to the next with a small transition. Each thing it can show is called a function, and you decide which functions are on, how long each stays, and in what order.

You set everything up from your phone or computer, on a settings site that the display hosts itself. There is nothing to install.

Set up your displayOpen the settings siteBrowse the functionsSend your RemindersGet help
Note

PixelPop connects to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks. If your router offers separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks, choose the 2.4 GHz one.

Get started

Set up your display

Power on, tell PixelPop which Wi-Fi to use, and you’re done. It takes about two minutes.

Connect to Wi-Fi

  1. Power on the display. It shows Connecting WiFi... while it looks for a network it already knows.
  2. The first time, there is no network to join, so it says No WiFi and then starts its own setup network.
  3. On your phone or computer, open Wi-Fi settings and join the network named PixelPop. It is open, with no password. The panel shows the name to look for.
  4. A setup page called PixelPop Wi-Fi Setup opens by itself. If it doesn’t, open a browser and go to 192.168.4.1, which the panel also shows.
  5. Choose your home network from the list, enter its password, and save. The display restarts and joins it.

See what it says

Once connected, PixelPop starts rotating through its functions. A ring of dots means it is waiting for a page’s first data, such as the weather. That usually takes a few seconds.

Tip

You only do the Wi-Fi setup once. PixelPop remembers your network, and remembers all your settings, even after it loses power.

Get started

Open the settings site

Every setting lives on a page the display serves over your home network. Open it from any phone, tablet or computer on the same Wi-Fi.

Find it

  1. On a device connected to the same Wi-Fi, open a browser and go to pixelpop.local.
  2. If that name doesn’t open, use the display’s number instead. Tap the BOOT button once and the panel shows its IP address for five seconds. Type it into the browser, for example 192.168.1.123.

The Home page

Home lists every function with a switch and a short live summary, such as 72°F, Pt cloudy. Use it to:

  • Turn functions on or off. At least one must stay on, otherwise the panel says Nothing turned on.
  • Change the order. Drag the ☰ handle up or down. The panel follows the same order.
  • Customize a function. Each has its own page, covered in the next chapters, with a ‹ Home link at the top to come back.

General settings

SettingWhat it does
BrightnessDims or brightens the whole panel, from 1 to 100.
Time zoneUsed by the clock, the calendar, the chimes and every time shown on the panel.
Screen paddingKeeps a border of blank pixels around the edge. Useful when the panel’s frame hides the outer row of LEDs. Content that reaches the edge is trimmed.
Screen transitionThe effect between pages. Choose one, or pick Random for a different one each time.
Transition speedHow quickly the effect plays.
Panel color orderOnly change this if colors look wrong, for example blue showing as green. Try the options until white looks white and blue looks blue.

Below the settings are three buttons. Refresh data now asks every function to fetch new data right away. Advanced opens tools for updating the firmware and checking how the display is doing (see Update the firmware). Change Wi-Fi network sends the display back to the setup network.

Buttons on the display

PressWhat happens
Tap BOOTShows the IP address for five seconds.
Hold BOOT for 5 secondsForgets the Wi-Fi network. The panel shows Resetting WiFi… and starts the setup network again.
Important

The settings site has no password. Anyone on your Wi-Fi network can open it, so use it on a network you trust.

Functions

Clock

The time in large digits, with the date beneath it.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
24-hour timeSwitches between 3:30 PM and 15:30.
Show the date (and AM/PM)Adds the weekday, the date and an A or P for the half of the day.
Seconds barThe thin line along the bottom edge that fills as the minute passes.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

The time comes from the internet and follows the time zone you chose on the Home page.

Functions

Weather

The temperature outside, with a picture of the sky.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
UnitsFahrenheit with miles per hour, or Celsius with kilometers per hour.
Details pageAdds the second page shown above.
LocationLatitude and longitude. The default is Chicago. To find yours, search for your address on any map site and read its coordinates.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Note

Weather data comes from Open-Meteo. If the first attempt fails, for example while your router is still starting up, PixelPop tries again after a few seconds and keeps trying. Its line on the Home page says why it has no data yet. Refresh weather now forces an update.

Functions

Forecast

The next few days at a glance, or one day in detail.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
LayoutTwo days per screen, or one day per screen.
Days to showOne to seven days.
Same location and units as WeatherOn by default, so changing your location on the Weather page changes the forecast too. Turn it off to use its own location and unit.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Functions

Air Quality

The temperature and humidity in the room where the display sits.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
Temperature unitFahrenheit or Celsius.
Correct a sensor that reads warmSubtracts up to 8 °C from the reading. Humidity is adjusted to match.
PagesChoose which of the three pages appear. Trend graphs show up after about 20 minutes of readings.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Tip

The sensor sits close to the processor and the panel driver, so it usually reads a few degrees warm. Leave the display running for half an hour, compare it with a thermometer you trust, and pick the difference in Correct a sensor that reads warm.

Note

PixelPop measures temperature and humidity only. It has no gas, particle or CO₂ sensor, so the readings describe comfort, not pollution.

Functions

Calendar

Your next events, one per page, with a colored band that tells you when.

The band across the top says when the event happens: IN 25 MIN, TODAY 3:30P, TOMORROW, WED 9:15P. Long titles wrap onto up to three lines.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
Published calendar addressThe public link of the calendar to show. See Show your calendar.
Look aheadHow far into the future to look for events.
Number of eventsEach event gets its own page.
All-day eventsInclude or hide them.
Events already startedKeep showing an event while it is under way.
24-hour timesSwitches between 3:30 PM and 15:30.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Repeating events are included. Times use the time zone chosen on the Home page.

Functions

Reminders

Things to do, most urgent first, with a blinking mark for the ones that matter.

Every reminder gets its own page. The reminder itself is one line of large letters. Under it, a small line gives the due date and the list it belongs to. Either line that is too long for the panel holds still for a moment, then scrolls sideways.

BandMeaning
RedOverdue. It says how long, for example OVERDUE 3D.
AmberDue today.
BlueDue later, or no date.

A blinking exclamation mark at the right end of the band marks a high-priority reminder.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
Which remindersOverdue and due today, due within 3 days, due within a week, or everything.
24-hour timesSwitches between 3:30 PM and 15:30.
Reminders with no due dateInclude them or leave them out.
Number of remindersEach one gets a page.
Blink the ! for overdue remindersHigh-priority reminders always blink. Turn this on to blink overdue ones too.
ALL CLEAR pageShows a check mark when there is nothing to do.
Hide the list if it has not been updatedStops showing old reminders if your phone hasn’t sent an update for a day or two.
The list nowThe reminders PixelPop currently holds. You can type or paste your own lines here to try it out.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Apple doesn’t let other devices read the Reminders app directly, so your iPhone, iPad or Mac sends the list to the display. Send your Reminders shows how.

Functions

Countdown

Days, hours and seconds until something you’re looking forward to.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
LabelUp to 10 characters, for example New Year or Birthday.
DateThe day to count down to.
Repeat every yearFor birthdays and holidays: after the date passes it counts to the next one.
Hide this page once the date has passedRemoves it from the rotation afterwards.
ShowMonths, days and hours:minutes:seconds, or days only.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

If the date has passed and you haven’t hidden the page, it counts up instead, with a + in front of the time.

Functions

Flights

Aircraft flying overhead, one at a time, nearest first.

Each page shows a callsign, the aircraft type, its altitude with a short status such as CLIMB or DESC, and its speed and distance from your chosen spot. An arrow shows the direction it is heading. When the airline’s logo is available, it appears at the top left.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
Center onPick a major airport from the list, or enter your own latitude and longitude.
Search radius5 to 100 nautical miles around that spot.
Most aircraft per roundOne to twelve, nearest first.
Hide aircraft on the groundOnly show flying aircraft.
Show a “no flights” screenA page that says so when nothing is in range.
Airline logoShow the logo at the top left, with an adjustable brightness.
New-flight tagA red corner tag on flights that have just appeared.
Flight statusShow climb, descent, cruise or emergency beside the altitude.
UnitsAviation (feet or flight level, knots, nautical miles), US (feet, mph, miles) or metric.
Update the listEvery 15 seconds, 30 seconds or minute.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Functions

News Ticker

Stock moves, headlines and currency rates in scrolling rows.

The ticker can show up to three rows at once: stock moves, headlines and currency conversion. A row appears once its data has arrived, and rows that are switched off give the others more room.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
RowsTurn each row on or off, and choose the small tag at the start of each (MARKETS, NEWS, FX).
Scroll speedSlow, normal or fast.
Stocks to watchUp to 15 symbols separated by commas. US stocks need only the symbol, such as AAPL.
Significant moveOnly stocks that moved at least this much are shown, biggest first. If fewer than three did, the three biggest movers are shown anyway.
UpdateEvery 5, 15 or 30 minutes.
Data fromStooq or Yahoo Finance. For other markets add the exchange suffix, such as VOD.UK on Stooq or VOD.L on Yahoo Finance.
News feedNPR, BBC World, BBC Business, BBC Technology, Google News, or your own RSS address (it must start with https://).
CurrencyThe currency to convert from, the ones to convert to (up to eight), and the amount. Rates are daily.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Prices are the latest the free service has, so outside market hours they show the last session.

Functions

Marquee

Your own message in lights, framed by marching dots.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
Line 1, 2 and 3Empty lines are skipped, so one line is shown large and centered when it fits. A line too wide for the panel pauses, then scrolls sideways.
Only show today’s messageThe message drops out of the rotation after the day you save it. Save the page again on a new day to show it that day.
AntsThe border: marching dashes, dots or long dashes, at slow, normal or fast speed, clockwise or counter-clockwise.

Every function also has Colors settings, so you can recolor its text and bands. Reset colors to default at the bottom of a page puts the originals back.

Tip

Good for “Dinner at 6”, “Happy birthday, Mia!” or “Shoes off, please.”

Functions

Photos

Your own pictures, shrunk to fit the panel.

Add up to 16 pictures from the Photos page. Your browser shrinks them before sending, so even large photos upload quickly.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
FitThe panel is twice as wide as it is tall, so most photos don’t match it exactly. Scale to fit stretches the picture, Crop fills the panel and trims the edges, and Black bars keeps the whole picture. This applies to every photo.
Photo brightnessHow bright pictures are, as a percentage.
Add photosPick one or more pictures. Delete a photo to make room once all 16 places are used.
Note

If the Photos page says the board has no storage area, choose a partition scheme that includes storage in the Arduino IDE (Tools › Partition Scheme) and upload again.

Functions

Chimes

Westminster bells or a cuckoo, on the quarter hour.

Chimes have no page on the panel. They play through the speaker at times you choose.

At the top of the page, Play the chimes switches them on or off. There is no screen time to set, because chimes only make sound.

SettingWhat it does
Chime styleWestminster (Big Ben): one phrase at :15, two at :30, three at :45, and the full chime with one bell strike per hour at :00. Or cuckoo: one call at :15, :30 and :45 and one cuckoo per hour.
When to chimeEvery minute (adds a short, quieter sound on the other minutes), every 15 minutes, or hourly only.
Volume1 to 100.
Active hoursUse the two-handle slider to choose the daily window when chimes can play. Presets include all day and 8am–8pm.
SpeakerThe onboard speaker, or an external I2S amplifier if you wired your own.
Test the soundButtons that play each chime right away, so you can check the volume.

Functions

Fireworks

A little show, with sound if you like.

The show restarts each time the page comes around, and runs for as long as Seconds on screen says.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
ColorsMulticolor, red white and blue, gold and white, or a color you pick.
How busySlow and calm, medium or busy.
FinaleA burst of rockets just before the page changes.
City skylineAdds a silhouette along the bottom.
SoundWhoosh, boom and crackle through the speaker, with its own volume.

Chimes take over the speaker when they are due.

Functions

Chomper

A tiny arcade chase, just for fun.

The whole story takes about ten seconds at normal speed. Set Seconds on screen to at least that to see all of it. It starts from the beginning each time the page comes around.

Each function’s page starts with two settings that work the same everywhere: Show in the rotation switches it on or off, and Seconds on screen sets how long it stays before the next one.

SettingWhat it does
SpeedSlow, normal or fast.
Show the scoreThe score at the top left.
Show the spare livesThe row of lives at the bottom left.
Maze wallsThe wall color.

Guides

Show your calendar

PixelPop reads a public link to your calendar. You share the calendar, copy the link, and paste it into the Calendar page.

On a Mac

  1. Open the Calendar app.
  2. In the sidebar, right-click the calendar you want to show and choose Share Calendar.
  3. Tick Public Calendar, then click Copy Link.

On iPhone, iPad or iCloud.com

  1. Open Calendar and tap the share button next to the calendar, or click the share icon next to it on iCloud.com.
  2. Switch on Public Calendar.
  3. Copy the link. It starts with webcal://.

Give the link to PixelPop

  1. Open the settings site and choose Calendar.
  2. Paste the link into Published calendar address.
  3. Choose how far ahead to look and how many events to show, then tap Save.
Important

Anyone who has the link can read that calendar, so keep it to yourself. Calendars from Google, Outlook and other services work too if you give their private .ics address.

The calendar refreshes in the background. Update the calendar now on the Calendar page fetches it right away.

Guides

Send your Reminders

Apple doesn’t let other devices read the Reminders app, so you make a Shortcut that sends your open reminders to PixelPop. You make it once, then it can run by itself.

Before you start

Open the Reminders page on the settings site. It shows your display’s address for this, ending in a private key, for example http://pixelpop.local/reminders/push?key=1a2b3c4d. Copy it. The key keeps other devices on your network from changing your list.

Make the shortcut

  1. Open Shortcuts and tap + to make a new shortcut. Name it “Send Reminders to PixelPop”.
  2. Add Find Reminders. Set the filter Is Completed to No. Sort by Due Date, earliest first, and turn Limit on with 20.
  3. Add Repeat with Each, using the found reminders. Inside it, add a Text action and build one line from the reminder’s Title, Due Date and List, each separated by | (space, bar, space). Tap the Due Date and set its Date Format to Custom with yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm.
  4. To mark urgent reminders, add an If inside the repeat: if the reminder’s Priority is High, add | ! to the end of the line.
  5. After the repeat, add Combine Text with New Lines, joining the Repeat Results.
  6. Add Get Contents of URL and paste the address. Tap Show More, set Method to POST, set Request Body to Form, and add one Text field named items whose value is the Combined Text.
  7. Run the shortcut once. The first time, allow it to reach devices on your local network. The Reminders page shows how many reminders arrived.
Tip

Reminders that have only a date and no time come out as 00:00. If that bothers you, use the date format yyyy-MM-dd for them.

Keep it up to date

In the Automation tab of Shortcuts, tap + and choose either:

  • App › Reminders › Is Closed, then Run Immediately with your shortcut. The display updates whenever you close Reminders after ticking something off.
  • Time of Day, for a few fixed times.

The request goes straight to the display over your home Wi-Fi, so it only works while your phone is on the same network. If an update is missed, the list stays as it was.

What each line can hold

One reminder per line: the title first, then any of the other parts after a bar, in any order. All of them are optional.

Buy milk | 2026-09-21 15:30 | Groceries
Call the dentist | 2026-09-22 | Health
Pay rent | 2026-09-01 | Home | !
Read a book
  • The due date is YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in your own time zone.
  • The list is the name of the list in Reminders.
  • A !, or the word high or urgent, marks a high-priority reminder.

You can also type or paste lines into the box on the Reminders page to see how they look.

Guides

Update the firmware

Install a new version of PixelPop from your phone or computer, with no USB cable. The Advanced page does it.

One-time preparation

Over-the-air updates need room for two copies of the firmware. The file partitions.csv, in the PixelPop folder next to PixelPop.ino, sets that up.

  1. In the Arduino IDE, open PixelPop and set Tools › Flash Size to 32MB.
  2. Connect the display with a USB cable and upload as usual. The IDE picks up partitions.csv by itself and ignores the Partition Scheme menu.
  3. Open the settings site and choose Advanced. Room for an update should show 6.0 MB.
Important

Changing the layout erases stored photos, so add them again afterwards. Every other setting stays.

Install an update

  1. In the Arduino IDE, choose Sketch › Export Compiled Binary. Find the file whose name ends in .ino.bin. Don’t use the ones with bootloader, partitions or merged in the name.
  2. On the Advanced page, press Show update code on the display. A four-digit code appears on the panel for half a minute.
  3. Type the code into the page, choose the .ino.bin file, and press Install firmware.
  4. Wait about a minute. The panel counts the kilobytes as they arrive, then restarts by itself.
Tip

The code appears only on the panel, so installing firmware takes someone standing at the display. Five wrong codes cancel it and a new one is needed. A code stays valid for five minutes.

If something goes wrong

  • “That is not a firmware file” or “different chip”: you picked the wrong file. Use the .ino.bin from Export Compiled Binary.
  • “No second firmware area”: the one-time preparation above has not been done yet.
  • The display doesn’t start after an update: connect it with USB and upload a working version from the Arduino IDE.

Versions

The firmware and every function have their own version number, such as 1.0.0. Each function’s page shows its number next to its name, and the Advanced page lists them all. That makes it easy to tell which build is on the display.

Diagnostics

Under the firmware card, the Advanced page shows uptime, Wi-Fi signal strength, free memory and the largest free block of memory. Secure downloads such as weather need a large free block. If it drops below about 40 KB, downloads can fail. Restart the display restarts it without a cable.

Help

If something looks wrong

Most problems show up as a message on the panel. Find it below.

On the panelWhat it means and what to do
Connecting WiFi...PixelPop is joining your network. Wait up to half a minute.
No WiFi
Starting setup...		It couldn’t join a network. Join the PixelPop Wi-Fi network on your phone and follow Set up your display. Check that your router is on and is a 2.4 GHz network.
WiFi setup
Join WiFi: PixelPop		Waiting for you. Join the network named PixelPop, then open 192.168.4.1 if the page doesn’t open by itself.
Scanning WiFi...Looking for nearby networks. It takes a few seconds.
Nothing turned onEvery function is off. Open the settings site and switch at least one on.
Resetting WiFi...You held BOOT for five seconds. PixelPop is forgetting its network and starting setup again.
A ring of dotsWaiting for the first data of a function, such as the weather. If it lasts more than a minute, open the settings site. Each function’s line on the Home page says what it is waiting for or why it failed. Weather and Forecast retry after a few seconds on their own.

Common questions

pixelpop.local doesn’t open.

Some networks and older devices can’t find a display by name. Tap BOOT, read the IP address on the panel, and type that into the browser instead.

A function doesn’t appear in the rotation.

Check that its switch is on, on the Home page. A function that has no data yet, such as a Calendar with no link, or a Weather page still waiting for its first reading, is skipped until it has something to show.

Colors are wrong, for example blue looks green.

Change Panel color order under General on the Home page until white looks white.

The temperature in Air Quality is too high.

The sensor sits near the processor. Use Correct a sensor that reads warm on its page.

No sound.

Check the volume on the Chimes or Fireworks page, and use Test the sound. Chimes take priority over Fireworks audio when they are due.

Reminders stop updating.

Your phone has to be on the same Wi-Fi network when the shortcut runs. Run it once by hand and check the count on the Reminders page. If you set Hide the list if it has not been updated, old reminders disappear after that time.

I want to start over with Wi-Fi.

Hold BOOT for five seconds, or tap Change Wi-Fi network at the bottom of the Home page.
